An external review of the Gates Foundation has found during their association, Bill Gates knew of Jeffrey Epstein's sex offence conviction. (AP: Jose Luis Magana)

An external review commissioned by the Gates Foundation has found Bill Gates and staff met with Jeffrey Epstein about 30 times between 2011 and 2014.

Mr Gates was aware of Epstein's 2008 sex offence conviction and heard staff concerns about the association, the review says.

The Microsoft co-founder says the review is an "important step in providing the clarity that partners, employees and grantees deserve".

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates and staff of his foundation met with notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein more than two dozen times, even as employees raised concerns about the reputational risk of working with him, an external review commissioned by the Gates Foundation has found.

The investigation conducted by law firm WilmerHale took five months to complete and involved more than 50 interviews with current and former Gates Foundation personnel, including Mr Gates.

It found between 2011 and 2014, about 30 meetings took place between Epstein and 10 foundation leaders and staff members.

There was no evidence the foundation paid Epstein or did anything illegal, according to a three-page summary released on Tuesday, US time.

Interest in the 20-year-old case has exploded in recent months even as US President Donald Trump has urged the public to move on from what he deems a "pretty boring" saga.

The review "also found no evidence of participation in, or knowledge of, Epstein's ongoing sex trafficking operations or criminal activities," the foundation said in a statement.

Epstein was convicted on state charges of soliciting a minor for prostitution and soliciting prostitution in 2008 and served 13 months in jail.

Mr Gates has not been accused of any crimes and has repeatedly expressed regret for his past association with Epstein.

The review said the foundation's primary engagement with Epstein involved two matters: a proposed donor-advised fund and a nonprofit called the International Peace Institute.

Epstein was introduced to Mr Gates and other foundation staff in 2011 by an advisor to both the foundation and Mr Gates's personal office, the WilmerHale review said.

The financier recommended Mr Gates establish a charitable investment fund to pool wealthy individuals' gifts for global public health.

Staff followed up with Epstein at Mr Gates's request on the legal considerations and tax benefits to donors.

An undated photo of Bill Gates and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor from the estate of Jeffrey Epstein. (Supplied: House Oversight Committee Democrats)

In December 2014, Epstein hosted a breakfast meeting at his Manhattan home with Mr Gates, along with foundation staff and potential donors, with the goal of securing investments to the fund.

But according to the review, Mr Gates concluded Epstein had "misrepresented" the donors' willingness to contribute and the foundation stopped working on the concept.

Epstein also brought together Mr Gates and the head of a non-profit that would eventually receive money from the foundation.

The review said in 2012, Epstein introduced Mr Gates to Terje Rød-Larsen, then the president of the International Peace Institute.

The Gates Foundation reached a grant agreement related to polio eradication with the International Peace Institute the following year.

Mr Rød-Larsen resigned in 2020 over his connections to Epstein.

Pilot Lawrence Visoski with Bill Gates in an undated photo from Jeffrey Epstein's estate. (Supplied: House Oversight Committee Democrats)

Throughout their interactions, Mr Gates knew about Epstein's sex offence conviction and heard concerns about their association from staff working with Epstein on the charitable investment fund, the review said.

Gates Foundation chief executive Mark Suzman said the board had approved measures that would strengthen its vetting process and risk management.

"The work we do depends on integrity and earning and maintaining the trust of partners," he said in a press release.

The Gates Foundation has been under scrutiny due to Mr Gates's association with Epstein.

Mr Gates's dealings with Epstein in a "personal capacity" were not investigated.

Investigators did not have access to the Microsoft billionaire's personal communications with the financier.

Still, Mr Gates said the review was an "important step in providing the clarity that partners, employees and grantees deserve".

A picture of Bill Gates with an unknown woman was released by the House Oversight Committee Democrats in December. (Supplied: House Oversight Committee Democrats)

His name appeared in a trove of documents relating to the US Department of Justice's investigation into Epstein released earlier this year.

They contained photos of Mr Gates posing with Epstein and women whose faces were redacted, as well as communication between the financier and the Gates Foundation's staff.

Mr Gates told Congress last month meetings with Epstein focused on possible philanthropy but proved fruitless, and the relationship ended by December 2014.

ABC/AP/Reuters
